solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Number of 20 briefly seen in South Carolina

definitions.text: Number of 20 briefly seen in South Carolina

parts.words: Number of 20 briefly seen in South Carolina
parts.note: a number is a song, the 20 are the Eagles; their famous song shortened to initials is H CA, and those letters run across 'soutH CArolina'

explanation.surface: A tour report: one of a band's songs was given a short airing at a concert in South Carolina.
explanation.walkthrough: The Eagles' signature song abbreviated is HCA, letters that sit side by side in 'South Carolina'; the blogger thought this thin, and nothing else in the clue builds the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eagles' best-known song, a 1977 title track, is one of the band's numbers, as 'number' means song.

clue.text: Faithful follower writes article supporting Henley & Schmit pieces

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting word sits underneath the rest
only pieces of the two surnames are kept, so most of their letters go

parts.note: Don Henley and Timothy B Schmit, two members of the Eagles
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A loyal fan writes a piece accompanying photos of two Eagles members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' keeps HEN from Henley and CHM from Schmit; 'writes' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A henchman is a loyal, often unquestioning, supporter or right-hand man.

clue.text: Like a stringed instrument? That's one of the 20 for you

definitions.meaning: fanciful adjective from harp plus the -y suffix, resembling that instrument
the 20 is the Eagles, read as birds: a species of large tropical eagle shares this name

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a thing resembles a harp and is told it is one of the eagles.
explanation.definitionFit: The harpy eagle is a big South American raptor; the question mark flags the invented adjective in the first sense.

clue.text: Singer sadly left boy band

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A vocalist, unhappily, quit a manufactured pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges L (left) with the letters of BOYBAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Dylan is the American singer-songwriter, famous since the 1960s folk revival.

clue.text: Chap with time to follow the 20

indicators.note: the time letter comes after the birds

parts.note: the 20 is the Eagles; taken as birds, eagles are ernes, a crossword staple

explanation.surface: A man who arrives later than the band to the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's first name, and any named man can stand for a chap.

clue.text: Ferrari? Darling, that's what VIPs get

parts.note: Ferraris are famously painted red
a Ferrari is a car
pet is an endearment like darling

explanation.surface: A celebrity's Ferrari, darling, is the kind of perk the very important receive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ferrari' gives two pieces: the classic racing red and the car itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrities and dignitaries are greeted with a carpet of that colour, so the phrase means lavish welcome treatment.

clue.text: Like one of the 20, longed to play?

indicators.note: letters set to play are free to move about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Was a musician aching to perform with the Eagles?
explanation.definitionFit: The golden eagle is a familiar species, so the adjective describes one kind of eagle.

clue.text: Don H & Patty S T-shirt, shortly to be modelled by stenographer

indicators.note: modelled means shaped anew, so the letters are remoulded
shortly cuts the final letter off the garment

parts.note: the casual top, spelt out

explanation.surface: Don Henley and Patty Smyth's T-shirt is soon to be worn on the catwalk by an office secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims T-shirt to TSHIR, and 'to be modelled' rearranges DONH, PATTYS and TSHIR; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stenographer takes dictation in quick symbols and then types it up, the old job title for that secretarial role.

clue.text: Perhaps one who saw Tommy Cooper (firm outing with one leaving)

indicators.note: outing means the company letters are put out of the surname

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
the article for one
a goer is one who goes, so one leaving

explanation.surface: Someone who watched the comedian Tommy Cooper, on a work outing, with a colleague walking out.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy Cooper was a British comedian, but here 'Tommy' is The Who's rock opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommy is a rock opera, so anyone in its audience is an example of a person who attends operas.

clue.text: It's hard to manage after retirement age

indicators.note: retirement means drawing back, so the word is read in the other direction

parts.note: to cope is to manage
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A pensioner complains that life is tough to handle once you stop working.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is an era or long period of history, which is one sense of an age.

clue.text: Fled in case bats flew, just missing head

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so the word is jumbled
the first letter is dropped

parts.note: sped means flew along

explanation.surface: Someone ran off in case the bats took flight, narrowly avoiding being hit on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' looks like the flying animals but means crazy, rearranging CASE to ESCA.
explanation.definitionFit: Escaped and fled are both past tenses for getting away from danger, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Expert now capable of delivering encryption requirement tips?

definitions.text: Expert now capable of delivering encryption requirement tips?

indicators.note: the tips of the words are their opening letters, read off in order

parts.words: Expert now capable of delivering encryption requirement

explanation.surface: Is a specialist ready to hand out advice on what secure coding needs?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a device or expert that can deliver encryption.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that turns plain text into cipher is what encryption needs, and that is a device that scrambles messages.

clue.text: Unconscious state, lacking heart

indicators.note: one of the two middle letters is removed

parts.note: the punctuation mark printed in the clue itself is named by its word

explanation.surface: A medical note: someone is out cold and has no heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed comma is part of the wordplay: its name loses one of its central Ms.
explanation.definitionFit: A coma is a prolonged state of deep unconsciousness, a direct medical synonym.

clue.text: Old women having left Crown & Thistle, drunk in ditch

indicators.note: drunk means reeling, so the letters stagger into a new order
the old women leave, so their letters go from the word

parts.note: O for old and W for women

explanation.surface: Elderly ladies leave two pubs, the Crown and the Thistle, and end up drunk in a ditch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having left' removes OW from CROWN leaving CRN; 'drunk' rearranges CRN with THISTLE. The Crown and Thistle sounds like a British pub name.
explanation.definitionFit: A slit trench is a narrow military trench for one or two soldiers, a kind of ditch.

clue.text: Need to get in matches for power cuts

indicators.note: the lack goes inside the matches

parts.note: bouts are boxing or wrestling matches
lack is a need or want

explanation.surface: Playing a fixture requires supply restoration after an electricity failure.
explanation.definitionFit: Blackouts are failures of electricity supply that leave an area dark.

clue.text: Large female eating a mixture of oil and fat

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: eating means taking something inside

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name

indicators.note: a mixture means the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A big woman consumes a blend of oil and fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oil and fat' reads as one phrase, but 'and' is a link and 'fat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanolin is the greasy wax from sheep's wool, a fatty substance used in creams.

clue.text: Betrayal of side in lost cause

indicators.note: a side of the word is one of its edge letters, here the end

parts.note: a reason is a cause

explanation.surface: Treachery by one team within a hopeless campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost cause' looks like a fixed phrase, but 'lost' gives only its edge letter and 'cause' stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Treason is the gravest betrayal, of one's country or sovereign.

clue.text: Section of Church Times covering vicar's bottom one month

indicators.note: the two letters cover the rest, one at each end

parts.note: T is time, so times gives two of them

indicators.note: the bottom of a word is its last letter

parts.note: an means one
Sep is short for September

explanation.surface: A page of the Church Times newspaper reports a clergyman's backside for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: The Church Times is a real Anglican newspaper, which hides that 'Church' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A transept is either arm of a cross-shaped church, a part of the building.

clue.text: Rabid royalist, like some of the 20

indicators.note: rabid means mad, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A fanatical monarchist resembles certain members of the Eagles.
explanation.definitionFit: The solitary eagle is a rare Central and South American raptor, so this adjective names some eagles.

clue.text: Glenn Frey, twice having stripped off, keeps cycling round beach to find something to eat

indicators.note: keeps is used in its sense of holding something in one's keeping, so the outer letters wrap round the rest
off means moved out of place, here shifting letters from one end to the other
stripping twice peels the outer letters off two times

parts.note: Glenn Frey was a founding member of the Eagles

indicators.note: letters go round in a cycle, moving from the front to the back

explanation.surface: Twice-naked Glenn Frey cycles round a beach looking for food.
explanation.walkthrough: Stripping 'Glenn Frey' twice removes its outer letters two times, leaving ENNFR, which 'off' moves round to FRENN; the commenters noticed that this move is itself a cycle, like the beach's.
explanation.definitionFit: The French bean is a green bean eaten as a vegetable, so it is food.

clue.text: Group dogs apart from bitches, initially

indicators.note: apart from means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: beagles are hunting dogs

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pack of hounds with the females kept separate, at first.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eagles are an American rock band, and a band is a musical group.

clue.text: More like one of the 20 found in top of beech tree

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter

parts.note: the alder is a tree

explanation.surface: Something resembling an Eagles member was spotted in the crown of a beech.
explanation.definitionFit: The bald eagle is America's national bird, so the comparative means more resembling that species.

clue.text: Even total failure returned boxes

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters read backwards
boxes means holds within, so the letters sit inside the phrase

explanation.surface: Even a complete flop sent back its packaging.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat and even both describe a level surface without bumps.

clue.text: Period of renewal's heaven for the 20's Joe

indicators.note: a period is a stretch taken from within something, here from the run of words

explanation.surface: A time of rebirth is bliss for the Eagles' guitarist.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Walsh joined the Eagles as guitarist in 1975, so he is the band's Joe.

clue.text: Paper girl's toy cat

parts.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
a doll is a classic girl's toy

explanation.surface: A newspaper story about a toy belonging to a girl's pet cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toy cat' looks like a single item, but 'toy' belongs with the girl and 'cat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ragdoll is a large, placid breed of domestic cat that goes limp when picked up.

clue.text: New business leading sheep

parts.note: a star is the leading performer
a tup is a ram, a male sheep

explanation.surface: A fresh agricultural venture with a prize ram at its head.
explanation.definitionFit: A start-up is a newly founded company, often a small tech firm.

clue.text: Not moving, as semi is rent-free

indicators.note: semi means half, so only the first of the two letters
free means loose, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A house that is static, since the semi-detached is let without charge.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is British for a semi-detached house; here 'semi' halves 'is' to I and 'free' rearranges RENT to NERT.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means motionless or lacking the power to move, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Europe's upset about Times and Sun revelations

indicators.note: about means around, so the anagram goes round the next letter
upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the word with its S counted
X is the multiplication sign, read as times
S is short for Sunday, the Sun's day

explanation.surface: The continent is upset by tabloid newspaper scoops in The Times and The Sun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges EUROPES to EPOSURE, which goes 'about' X.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposures are disclosures of scandal or wrongdoing, things revealed to the public.
